transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep forgetting things I’m supposed to follow up on—scheduled callbacks, work orders, stuff I told people I’d take care of. It’s gotten bad enough that things are piling up at work, and they basically sent me here because I could lose my chance at moving up if I don’t get it handled.
Have you experienced this kind of forgetfulness and trouble following through on tasks since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

No, it’s not new. I remember being like this back in grade school, way before any work pressure. Teachers would say I was bright, but I was always losing papers, missing parts of directions, or needing reminders to actually finish my classwork.
Aside from the forgetfulness, do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things—like work, health, or everyday situations—more than you feel you should?

I’m not really sure I’d call it excessive worrying. I mean, I get stressed when I forget things or when work is on me about it, but I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about everything like my health or everyday stuff all the time.
Do you often feel restless, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?
I don’t really know. I don’t think I’m especially restless or impulsive, at least not that I’ve noticed. Sitting still isn’t usually the thing people complain about with me.
Do you notice this same forgetfulness and trouble finishing tasks happening at home or in other parts of your life, not just at work?

Yes, it’s not just work. I mean, work is where it’s really catching up with me—forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and follow-ups I told people I’d do. But it happens outside of that too, just with regular stuff I’m supposed to keep track of. It’s gotten bad enough that everything’s piled up, and work basically told me I needed to come in before I mess up my chance to move up.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities—like managing multiple steps of a project or keeping your workspace and belongings in order?
I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I can get messy or lose track of what I’m doing, but I don’t know if it’s really an organizing problem the way you mean. I’d probably need an example.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things going on around you—like noises or other activities—when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yes. That happens a lot. Like I’ll start a digital work order thinking I understand what I’m supposed to do, and then halfway through reading the notes there’s a noise or I think about the next job, and my mind just kind of goes off. Then I look back and realize I don’t even know what I just read.
Do you often lose or misplace things you need, like keys, phone, or paperwork, or forget everyday commitments such as appointments or errands?

Yes, all the time. I’m constantly looking for the tablet, my keys, the flashlight, or some tool I literally just had in my hand a minute ago. It gets embarrassing because it holds up the job, and I know it makes me look careless, even when I’m trying not to be.
